classification.difficultyReason: Generalises the opposite-bearing rule to algebraic expressions in two bearing ranges.

content.prompt: A true bearing is $a^{\circ}$. Write an expression for the true bearing of the opposite direction of $a^{\circ}$ if:

spec.description: Four black compass arrows meet at O. A blue southeast ray and a blue clockwise arc from north show the given bearing a°.
spec.mathematics: The illustrated ray represents a bearing strictly between 0° and 180°; its drawn direction is schematic and supplies no numerical bearing.
spec.answerVisibility: The given ray, arc and a° label remain visible. The opposite-bearing expression is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The opposite direction is half a turn away. Since $a$ is between $0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$, add $180^{\circ}$:
$$\text{Opposite bearing}=(a+180)^{\circ}.$$

spec.description: Four black compass arrows meet at O. A blue southwest ray and a blue clockwise reflex arc from north through east and south show the given bearing a°.
spec.mathematics: The illustrated ray represents a bearing strictly between 180° and 360°; its drawn direction is schematic and supplies no numerical bearing.
spec.answerVisibility: The given ray, reflex arc and a° label remain visible. The opposite-bearing expression is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The opposite direction is half a turn away. Since $a$ is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$, subtract $180^{\circ}$:
$$\text{Opposite bearing}=(a-180)^{\circ}.$$
